key_insight: The paper generates realistic polycrystalline microstructures by combining flow matching with a C4-equivariant graph neural network over anisotropic power-diagram representations.
engineering_relevance: This enables fast, resolution-flexible synthesis of microstructure samples for materials design and property modeling without requiring costly EBSD acquisition.
method: Encode microstructures as anisotropic power diagrams to obtain a compact geometric representation.
Train a flow-matching generative model on graph neural networks with built-in 90° rotational equivariance (C4).
Use training-free guidance to steer generation toward desired microstructure styles such as welds, slabs, and 3D-printed alloys.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports successful generation of diverse, realistic-looking microstructures, including copper weld, cast metal slab, 3D-printed stainless steel, and heterogeneous lamella titanium examples.
watch_item: Realistic rendering and guidance depend on the quality of the geometric parameterization and objective design, so physical fidelity and generalization beyond the shown examples may require careful validation.
paper_title: $C_4$-Equivariant Flow Matching on Anisotropic Power-Diagram Graphs for Microstructure Generation
